sections.title: What a healthy self looks like

items.q: If mental health isn't just "no symptoms," what is it?
items.a: A **healthy self**: sound **structure of self** plus **function of self** that yields **agency and gratitude** — empowerment to act plus humility to appreciate what is.

items.q: How much of the mind is unconscious in Conti's model?
items.a: Picture an **iceberg**: the conscious tip sits above water, but maybe **~95%** is unconscious biological processing beneath. Conscious work is awareness, choice, and integration — not total control.

items.q: What belongs in the structure of self?
items.a: **Unconscious content**, **defense mechanisms**, **character structure** (predispositions + action patterns), and **self-concept**. Diagnose this architecture before chasing surface behaviors.

items.q: What does the function of self include?
items.a: **Self-awareness**, **salience** (what you choose to notice), how you **deploy defenses**, and striving via drives. Mental health includes placing attention on what matters instead of reactive fixation.

items.q: Which drive puts "rubber to the road" for flourishing?
items.a: The **generative drive** — create, understand, explore, contribute. Aggressive drive (assertion) and pleasure drive (enjoyment) are necessary but insufficient alone.

items.q: What happens when aggressive and pleasure drives go wrong?
items.a: When they dominate or collapse you get **envy/destruction** at one pole or **demoralization** (low agency, failure to launch) at the other — generative striving is the north star for balance.

items.q: Why isn't "I'm not confident" a useful global label?
items.a: Confidence is **state-dependent** — strong in many domains, fragile in one. Map the specific **cupboard** (unconscious pattern, narrative, defense) instead of relabeling identity.
**Spirited inquiry**: look in **all the cupboards** — childhood, defenses, drives, relationships, biology — before medicating or concluding. Medicine supports exploration; it doesn't replace it.

items.q: How should you treat overthinking and negative self-talk?
items.a: Rumination and procrastination often signal **drive imbalance** or defense loops. Audit **negative internal dialogue**, restructure self-talk, and notice which defense (projection, displacement, sarcasm) runs when.
